title: Check yourself: Choosing in practice: scenarios, reasons and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A task reads forty log files and looks up each failing job in the company's tracker, which needs a login. What does the page place first?

options.text: A subagent, because the reading would flood the conversation
options.says: Ruled out because "a subagent alone cannot reach the tracker".

options.text: An MCP server, because only a connection can reach that system
options.says: The page says MCP "gives Claude purpose-built tools for an external system, with the connection and authentication handled by the server".

options.text: A skill, because it can hold the tracker's address and steps
options.says: Ruled out because "a skill is knowledge and cannot make the connection".

options.text: A hook, because it fires each time a job fails
options.says: Ruled out because a hook answers "Must it happen, or be blocked, every time with no judgment?", which the task does not state.

questions.stem: Six repositories must all give Claude the same commit-message style, and engineers forget to ask for it. Where does the style belong?

options.text: In a plugin shared by the six
options.says: Ruled out because "a plugin cannot carry it, since its instruction file is not loaded as context".

options.text: In an instruction file kept in each project
options.says: The page says an instruction file is the answer for a convention that is "always-known", and row 14 gives it for six repositories.

options.text: In an MCP server that stores the style guide
options.says: Ruled out because "MCP is how a session reaches a system that is not on the machine", and a style guide is not such a system.

options.text: In a skill whose description mentions commits
options.says: Ruled out because "a skill is loaded only if its description matches the task, so the mistake can repeat".

questions.stem: An application that calls the Messages API must let Claude read a calendar service. The vendor offers an MCP endpoint for it, and the team wants no login of its own to maintain. Which choice does the page give?

options.text: A skill describing the calendar's operations
options.says: Ruled out because "a skill is knowledge and cannot make the connection".

options.text: A tool the team defines, with its own schema and code
options.says: Ruled out because rebuilding it as your own tool "repeats work and owns its login".

options.text: The connector, aimed at the hosted offer
options.says: The page says that in an application a hosted server "can be reached through the connector", with the reason `remote-server`.

options.text: A hook that calls the calendar before each request
options.says: Ruled out because "no Claude Code extension exists in an API call", and a hook is one.
